This hybrid meeting is taking place via Microsoft Teams & at the Girdwood Community Room, 250 Egloff Rd:

The Girdwood Board of Supervisors is subject to the Alaska Open Meetings Act as found in Alaska Statute 44.62.310
and Anchorage Municipal Code1.25 - Public Meetings.
The Girdwood Board of Supervisors operates under the Girdwood Public Meetings Standards of Conduct.

Call to Order 7:00 p.m. Mike Edgington, Co-Chair

Land Acknowledgement: The Girdwood Board of Supervisors acknowledges the indigenous peoples of Alaska, whose land we
reside on. The community of Girdwood, situated between the areas known to be Dena'ina and Alutiiq homeland, respects the people
who were stewards of this land for generations. We commit to the continued stewardship of this land and are grateful to be part of a
wider community that seeks to maintain a sustainable use of Girdwood Valley for present and future peoples.

OLD BUSINESS:
6. MOA Legal Dept update to clarify private vs public interests under Ethics Code and GBOS actions at the January Regular Meeting.
    (Zach Schwartz, Assistant Municipal Attorney)
    Motion: GBOS moves to limit item to 30 Minutes BS/KO  Assent
    Motion: GBOS moves to limit item to 15 minutes KO/JW  Assent

    Following January meeting, ME requested legal assistance related to disclosure and recusal of private vs public interests.
    Assistant Municipal Attorney states that prior opinions from Board of Ethics is that members of Assembly serve on other boards in
    Anchorage without need for disclosure of private interest. Private interests are distinct from public role. In code, there is no conflict
   when someone is discharged with two separate duties within the Municipality.
   Members of the Assembly seeking office of the chair are not required to recuse themselves from that vote. This can be extended to
    broader interpretation; member is not required to recuse themselves from votes.

    Action in January was to revote after GBOS members challenged that Mike Edgington’s private interest in Federation of
    Community Councils created need for him to disclose and be recused from action on the FCC item before GBOS, which was
     originally voted on in November. Attorney does not have legal advice on how to resolve the outcome of the January meeting.

    Chair switches to JW so that ME can make motion regarding Item #6:



                                                                                         2

Motion:
   GBOS moves to put aside the decision in January as it was predicated on declaring private interest when it was a public action.
   ME/BS
    Motion carries 3-2 in roll call vote (Y=BB, BS, ME; N=JW, KO)

    Legal opinion is that there was no conflict requiring disclosure and recusal. GBOS can either vote to vacate that decision or send it
     to the ethics board for review. Some members of GBOS are interested in Board of Ethics review of the item. Group reviews the
    motion: vacate the January GBOS vote. This will return the vote to the decision from November.

   BB requests to be recused from the vote as he did not attend in January. This request is denied; voting is a responsibility of GBOS
    unless specific conditions are met.

    Attorney departs the meeting when no further questions are asked. Group begins to move to item #7.

   ME returns to chair.

   JW states that ME should not have been allowed to vote on the prior vote, revisiting the conflict of interest item and his recusal on
     that item in January. ME states that the presentation from the municipal attorney confirmed no private conflict of interest in similar
    scenarios. Recusal of ME in January was incorrect. Vote at tonight’s meeting corrects that error.

    Motion:
   GBOS moves to reconsider the vote that was just taken.
    Motion by KO. Reconsideration motion must come from someone on the prevailing side. No motion is made by member of
     prevailing side.

    Motion:
   JW moves to challenge ruling of the chair.
    Motion by JW/KO
   No vote on this is taken, however topic changes to point of order as member believes that the information provided before the vote
      is different from the action after the vote.

    Group reviews the motion that was made and voted on.
   No motion to reconsider is made by members on the prevailing side.

7.  Consider requesting amendment to 2026-0032 Amend AMC 21.05 and 21.15 to ease restrictions on agricultural uses and food
    production in Anchorage Bowl to include Chapter 9/Girdwood. (Edgington)
    https://www.muni.org/CityViewPortal/Planning/Status?planningId=18347

    Motion:
   GBOS moves to postpone this item to GBOS April meeting, at which time a draft resolution for it can be considered.

    Motion carries by Assent

8. GHEC Recommendation for GBOS support of RFP for a Housing Action and Implementation Plan NTE $100,000 from the GHEC
    Budget (Chandler/Edgington)

    Motion:
   GBOS moves to approve request for RFP for Housing Action and Implementation Plan RFP based on the draft provided by GHEC,
    not to exceed $100,000.
    Motion by BB/BS
    Motion carries 5-0 in roll call vote.

   RFP will be finalized by MOA purchasing department. With approval of motion, Kyle will find direction with municipal structure for
    housing. BB requests that a broader sample of communities is studied, finding communities of similar characteristics and proximity
     to big cities and workforce there. He notes that Breckenridge and other resort communities are an easy commute from large
    population centers.

10. GTC request for GBOS Resolution of Support for an Anchorage Park Foundation Grant application for interpretive signs at the
    Glacier Creek Bridge. Grant is matching 1:1, currently estimating $30K total: $15K from APF and $15K that is cumulative of in-kind,
   GTC non-profit funds and Parks and rec funds.(Burnett)

   One whereas will be revised to address that we don’t currently have dates for construction of the bridge, however award of the
    contract is imminent. Grant span is 2 years, creation of the signs can occur within that timeframe.

    Motion:
   GBOS moves to accept the resolution of support for APF Grant.
    Motion by BB2nd KO
    Motion carries 5-0 in roll call vote

11. GHEC Vacancy (Edgington)
   No applications for GHEC have been received.
   GHEC considered but rejected the idea of changing the number of members in their Operating Rules to 5 instead of 7, citing that
    they had been successful in achieving a quorum even with only 5 active members.
    Item will be moved to notices on GBOS agenda for administrative action.

12. Alyeska Highway speed limit and engineering enhancements related to speed limit
    Scott Thomas with DOT has retired and before leaving recommended that the Alyeska Highway speed is reduced from 45 to 40
   MPH and that the 30MPH zone is extended, however the DOT intent to complete engineering enhancements that were
   recommended to accompany the speed limit change is not known. Without those modifications and education, the responsibility for
    education would fall solely on Whittier Police via enforcement, which would not be positive.

    Group determines that having a meeting with DOT and LUC to discuss Alyeska Highway modifications and speed limits would be
     helpful. Group discusses holding a joint GBOS LUC meeting with DOT once the new board is set and when DOT is available. Staff
      will coordinate.
